pages.quiz:
ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13
====

GRADE: Grade 2
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Connected text reading and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text reading and fluency.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Connected text reading and fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text reading and fluency.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Connected text reading and fluency.

2. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. blue
   C. quickly
   D. run

3. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.

4. When practising Pre-reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pre-reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Pre-reading.

5. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

6. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. went
   C. going
   D. goed

7. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. No full stops

8. When practising Word reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Word reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Word reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Word reading.

9. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. Where is the library
   C. Where is the Library
   D. where is the library

10. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only an action
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only a describing word

11. When practising Language structures School, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Language structures School.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language structures School.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Language structures School.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Language structures School.

12. When practising Letter sound knowledge, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Letter sound knowledge.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Letter sound knowledge.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Letter sound knowledge.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Letter sound knowledge.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Attentive listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text reading and fluency.

2. D — run

3. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-reading.

5. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

6. B — went

7. B — One main idea with supporting sentences

8. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word reading.

9. A — Where is the library?

10. C — A person, place, thing, or idea

11. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language structures School.

12. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Letter sound knowledge.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Punctuation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Guided Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Attentive listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pronunciation and Vocabulary; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
